family_history: Mother: cerebral aneurysm (repaired surgically at age 52)

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden severe headache 8 hours ago, now partially improved, transferred from outside hospital
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Mitchell is a 45-year-old male with poorly controlled hypertension who presents after transfer from an outside hospital where he was evaluated for a sudden severe headache that began approximately 8 hours ago. He reports that the headache came on within seconds while he was driving, describing it as the worst headache of his life, rated 10/10 at onset. He vomited once before calling his wife, who drove him to the nearest emergency department. At the outside hospital, a non-contrast CT head was performed and reportedly read as negative by the emergency physician. He was given IV fluids, ondansetron, and ketorolac, after which the headache improved somewhat to 5/10. However, his wife expressed concern and insisted on transfer to a tertiary center because his mother had a cerebral aneurysm. On arrival here, he remains uncomfortable but improved compared to the maximal onset. He reports mild residual neck stiffness and is sensitive to the light in the examination room. He denies focal weakness, vision changes, speech difficulty, or any preceding sentinel headaches. He has had occasional headaches in the past that he attributes to stress, but states these were never of this severity or acuity. He takes ibuprofen for those headaches and his blood pressure has not been well managed. He has not had a neurological examination or brain imaging previously.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; somewhat anxious; GCS 15; mild photophobia
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 4mm, brisk; visual fields full; EOM intact; no papilledema on fundoscopy; no ptosis; facial sensation and movement symmetric
neurological_exam.motor: 5/5 strength throughout all four extremities; no pronator drift
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick all extremities
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric throughout; plantar responses flexor bilaterally
neurological_exam.additional: Nuchal rigidity present: chin-to-chest restricted by 2 finger-breadths; Kernig sign positive; Brudzinski sign equivocal; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Thin layering of hyperdense blood in the left Sylvian fissure, easily missed on initial review
Subtle hyperdensity in the suprasellar cistern and left perisylvian region

additional_observations: Fisher grade 2 pattern - thin subarachnoid blood
Initial read by OSH radiologist reported as negative - findings are subtle
ct.impression: Thin subarachnoid hemorrhage in the left Sylvian fissure and suprasellar cistern consistent with Fisher grade 2 SAH. Findings are subtle and may have been overlooked on initial review. No hydrocephalus. Urgent CTA recommended for aneurysm evaluation.
recommended_actions: Immediate CTA head and neck for aneurysm evaluation
Lumbar puncture if clinical suspicion remains high and CTA negative

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 13.2 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 148 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.18 ng/mL (H), BNP 142 pg/mL (H).

cell_count.comment: Non-clearing bloody CSF across all tubes - traumatic tap excluded

special_tests.Xanthochromia: Present on visual inspection and spectrophotometry

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 24 cmH2O. WBC: 180/uL (corrected for blood) (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 168 mg/dL (elevated, normal <45 mg/dL). Glucose: 78 mg/dL (serum glucose 148, ratio 0.53 - normal) (ratio 0.53). Xanthochromia: Present on visual inspection and spectrophotometry. findings: Deep symmetric T-wave inversions in leads V1-V5 (neurogenic T-waves)
ecg.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia with deep symmetric T-wave inversions V1-V5 and QTc prolongation. Must be distinguished from primary cardiac event.

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm measuring 4.8 x 4.2 mm with irregular lobulation and daughter sac

output.impression: 4.8 mm saccular aneurysm at left MCA bifurcation with irregular morphology and daughter sac, consistent with ruptured aneurysm. No additional aneurysms. Left Sylvian fissure subarachnoid hemorrhage correlates with aneurysm location. Recommend conventional DSA for endovascular treatment planning.
recommended_actions: Conventional DSA for definitive aneurysm characterization
Endovascular coiling or microsurgical clipping decision by neurovascular team

output.wall_motion: Apical hypokinesis with basal hyperkinesis - pattern consistent with Takotsubo/stress cardiomyopathy
findings: Apical ballooning pattern with apical hypokinesis
output.impression: Takotsubo stress cardiomyopathy (neurogenic Takotsubo) in the setting of subarachnoid hemorrhage. EF mildly reduced at 52%. Apical ballooning pattern consistent with catecholamine-mediated myocardial stunning. Expect recovery with supportive care.
recommended_actions: Avoid excessive fluid restriction - balance against neurogenic pulmonary edema risk
Repeat echo in 4-6 weeks to confirm recovery

output.impression: TCD day 1 post-SAH shows no vasospasm. Velocities within normal limits. Daily TCD monitoring recommended days 4-14 as vasospasm risk peaks. Left MCA velocities will be closely watched given ipsilateral aneurysm location.
recommended_actions: Maintain euvolemia (triple-H therapy if vasospasm develops)

findings.description: TTP mildly prolonged compared to right hemisphere

output.impression: CT perfusion shows borderline reduction in CBF in left MCA territory without established infarction (CBV preserved). Pattern suggests early hemodynamic compromise but not yet delayed cerebral ischemia. Monitor closely. If clinical deterioration, consider intra-arterial therapy.
recommended_actions: Maintain systolic BP 160-200 mmHg if vasospasm developing
Consider intra-arterial verapamil or angioplasty if refractory vasospasm

findings.finding: Ruptured saccular aneurysm 4.8 mm confirmed; irregular lobulation; neck 3.1 mm
Endovascular coiling performed: complete aneurysm occlusion achieved (Raymond class I)
No residual aneurysm filling; parent artery patent

output.impression: Successful endovascular coiling of left MCA bifurcation aneurysm with complete occlusion. Parent artery and branches preserved. No procedure-related complications. Follow-up DSA at 6 months recommended to assess for recanalization.

output.proposed: Nimodipine 60 mg orally every 4 hours for 21 days
interactions: Lisinopril + nimodipine: additive hypotensive effect - monitor BP closely
warnings: Must not crush and inject IV - fatalities reported
Monitor for hypotension, hold if SBP <100 mmHg
Hold antihypertensives during triple-H therapy for vasospasm
output.formulary_status: Available - brand Nymalize oral solution or generic capsules
alternatives: No equivalent alternative with proven vasospasm prevention efficacy

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from left MCA bifurcation aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 2)

differential.key_features: CSF shows non-clearing bloody tap with xanthochromia, CT shows blood - definitively SAH
CTA shows saccular aneurysm, not arterial beading; CSF bloody
Non-clearing RBCs across tubes 1-4 (138,000-142,000) and xanthochromia exclude traumatic tap
CSF bloody with xanthochromia, no neutrophilic pleocytosis, glucose normal ratio

optimal_actions.action: Urgent repeat non-contrast CT head (or review OSH images with neurovascular radiologist)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Subtle Fisher grade 2 SAH in left Sylvian fissure missed at OSH

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture given high clinical suspicion despite initial CT read as negative
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Non-clearing bloody CSF with xanthochromia confirming SAH

optimal_actions.action: Interpret labs - check troponin, coagulation, sodium, glucose
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild troponin elevation (neurogenic), stress leukocytosis, normal coagulation

optimal_actions.action: Analyze ECG - assess for neurogenic cardiac changes
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Neurogenic T-wave inversions V1-V5, QTc prolongation

optimal_actions.action: Urgent CTA head for aneurysm identification
optimal_actions.expected_finding: 4.8 mm left MCA bifurcation aneurysm with irregular morphology
Safe with monitoring; hold if hypotension

optimal_actions.action: Order echocardiogram to assess neurogenic cardiac injury
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Takotsubo pattern with apical hypokinesis - neurogenic cardiomyopathy

critical_actions: Perform LP despite negative OSH CT - SAH cannot be excluded without LP within first 12 hours
CTA head and neck immediately after SAH confirmed
Start nimodipine within 4 hours of SAH diagnosis for vasospasm prophylaxis
Monitor and manage sodium closely (cerebral salt wasting/SIADH risk)
contraindicated_actions: Do not discharge without LP when clinical presentation strongly suggests SAH despite negative CT
Do not give NSAIDs (ibuprofen) - increased bleeding risk post-SAH
Do not allow patient to be normotensive post-SAH without aneurysm secured if vasospasm suspected
Do not administer nimodipine intravenously - life-threatening cardiovascular collapse
Do not perform LP without CT first to rule out mass lesion causing herniation risk
key_reasoning_points: The key diagnostic challenge: CT was reportedly negative at OSH but LP showing non-clearing bloody CSF with xanthochromia is definitive for SAH
Non-clearing RBCs (142,000 tube 1 vs 138,000 tube 4) distinguishes SAH from traumatic tap - traumatic tap shows clearing
Xanthochromia develops 2-4 hours after ictus and persists for weeks - confirms subarachnoid blood
Family history of cerebral aneurysm (mother) increases index of suspicion - first-degree relatives have 3-5x increased risk
Neurogenic ECG changes (T-wave inversions, QTc prolongation) are common in SAH and should not trigger cardiac catheterization
Troponin elevation in SAH context is neurogenic (catecholamine surge) unless clinical picture suggests primary cardiac event
Hunt-Hess 2 (headache and meningism only) predicts better outcome than grades 3-5
Left MCA aneurysm with left Sylvian fissure blood demonstrates the importance of correlating aneurysm location with hemorrhage distribution
